title: IBM to deploy India’s first quantum computer in Amaravati early 2027
source_used: The Economic Times, full text read on ET Infra (14 Oct 2026); the main ET page shows only the first lines
key_facts: IBM plans to deploy what it describes as India's largest quantum computer early next year (2027) at the newly developed tech park in Amaravati, a top executive said.
The facility will focus on practical applications of quantum computing and on helping Indian enterprises prepare their IT infrastructure for post-quantum cryptography.
Sandip Patel, managing director of IBM India, told ET: "I think the facility is almost ready... Machines should be here early next year."
The project, backed by chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu, is part of IBM's Andhra Pradesh Quantum Valley initiative, executed with Tata Consultancy Services.
Patel said building the infrastructure is only one part of the task and that developing applications and the skills to use the machine is equally important.
He said real-world quantum applications are still three to five years away.
NITI Aayog, the government policy think tank, says India will need to train some 100,000 quantum developers to be a leader in the 2030s.

As an example, HSBC and IBM reported a trial that improved predictions of whether European corporate bond trades would be executed at a quoted price by up to 34 per cent versus common classical techniques.

why_it_matters_hint: India would host a large IBM quantum machine from 2027 and wants applications and post-quantum security preparation to grow around it.
notes: The headline of the ET article says 'India's first quantum computer' but its text says IBM describes it as 'India's largest'; the entry follows the text. The plan and the date are one executive's statement; no machine specification or cost is given.
